monthly_review.summary: This month shows a deliberate shift toward lower-intensity, higher-volume aerobic development — evidenced by increased Z1/Z2 time, reduced average HR, and slightly slower average pace — while maintaining VO2 max and improving running efficiency metrics.
monthly_review.highlight: Zone distribution shifted dramatically: Z1+Z2 time increased from 55% to 83%, while Z4+Z5 dropped from 19% to 1% — indicating a strategic, recovery-focused aerobic base rebuild.

goal_tracker.message: You need 0.2 more km across 1 session in the remaining 5 days to match last month’s distance — easily achievable with a short 2–3 km Zone 1 recovery run.

insights.title: Efficiency dipped slightly despite lower HR
insights.body: Aerobic efficiency decreased from 13.66 to 13.39 km/hr per bpm this month, even as average HR fell 7 bpm — suggesting that the slower pace (558 vs 532 sec/km) outpaced HR reduction, possibly due to fatigue or form drift on longer efforts.

insights.title: Near-total elimination of threshold and VO2 max work
insights.body: Z4+Z5 time dropped from 19% (7.2 min/run avg in Apr) to just 1% (0.6 min/run avg in May), meaning no meaningful stimulus for lactate buffering or maximal oxygen uptake — sustainable for recovery but not for progression if prolonged.

insights.title: Cadence improved while ground contact time stabilized
insights.body: Avg cadence rose from 142 to 145 spm, and ground contact time held steady at ~310 ms (313 → 309 → 286 → 316 → 308 ms across recent runs), suggesting better neuromuscular coordination without sacrificing stability — especially notable on the 2.5 km Z3 effort (286 ms, 145 spm, 7.45 min/km).

insights.title: Aerobic Training Effect declined despite higher Z1/Z2 volume
insights.body: Avg aerobic TE fell from 3.1 to 2.7, even with +28% more time in Z1/Z2 — likely because most runs stayed below 135 bpm (e.g., May 20: 132 bpm, 5.6 km) and lacked cumulative duration or intensity 'dose' needed to elicit stronger aerobic adaptation.

recommendations.action: Do one 6 km Zone 2 run at 135–142 bpm (target avg HR = 138 bpm) within the next 3 days, using your May 12 run (138 bpm, 5.5 km) as pacing reference.
recommendations.reason: This bridges the aerobic TE gap — your last Zone 2 run at 138 bpm yielded 2.8 TE; extending to 6 km at same HR will likely lift avg TE back toward 3.0+.

recommendations.action: Insert one 8-minute Z3 interval session: 4 x 2 min @ 148–152 bpm (like your May 16 effort), with 90 sec walk/jog recovery between.
recommendations.reason: Reintroduces targeted lactate threshold stimulus after zero Z4/Z5 time this month — critical to prevent aerobic efficiency decay and maintain pace resilience.

recommendations.action: Perform a 3 km barefoot or minimalist-shoe stride drill session focusing on landing under center of mass: aim for cadence ≥152 spm and vertical oscillation ≤7.5 cm (your recent avg is 7.7 cm).
recommendations.reason: Your vertical oscillation trended upward (7.5→8.1→7.5 cm) while stride length varied widely (67.6→94.4→67.6 cm); this suggests overstriding on fatigued runs — correcting it will improve efficiency and reduce injury risk.

weekly_focus.description: Re-establish the link between heart rate discipline, pace control, and neuromuscular efficiency — prioritizing consistency in Zone 2 HR, intentional cadence, and brief but precise Z3 efforts to recalibrate your body's response to moderate intensity.
suggested_sessions: 3 km form-focused strides (≥152 spm, ≤7.5 cm VO)
